name: Maroczy Bind

plans.label: Occupy d5
plans.description: Plant a knight on the hole in front of the bind, where both bind pawns guard it and no Black c-pawn exists to challenge it.

success.note: A White knight stands on d5 and the square is a Tabiya-detected White outpost. The detector is strict: while Black keeps an e-pawn able to reach e6, d5 is not yet an outpost, which matches the chess - the clamp only counts once the evicting break is spent.

plans.label: Hold the bind with both breaks unplayed
plans.description: Restrain both freeing breaks and improve pieces behind the pawn wall: the bind still stands and no Black pawn has reached b5 or d5.

success.note: RESTATED PLAN. The plan was 'Squeeze on space', whose success was the continued absence of both breaks. It is now the present-tense version: the bind is still on the board and neither freeing pawn has reached b5 or d5. Read at the end of a run this says the breaks did not land; it cannot say they never will. Original success note: 'Restraint is the continued absence of opposing breaks and is not decidable from one position.'

plans.label: Get the pawn to b5
plans.description: Prepare the queenside break with the a-pawn and rook support: a pawn reaches b5 while the c4 pawn still stands.

success.note: RESTATED PLAN. The plan was 'The b5 break', whose success was declined because the recaptures vary. It is now whether the lever arrived: a Black pawn stands on b5 while the bind's c4 pawn is still there to be hit. Original success note: 'The break's recapture shapes vary too widely for one arithmetic expression.'

plans.label: Get the pawn to d5
plans.description: Prepare the central break to dissolve the bind in one stroke, usually after heavy preparation: the d-pawn reaches d5.

success.note: RESTATED PLAN. The plan was 'The d5 break', whose success was declined because the recaptures vary. It is now whether the break arrived: the pawn stands on d5 and has left d6. Original success note: 'The break's recapture shapes vary too widely for one arithmetic expression.'

plans.label: Remove the dark-squared bishop or plant a knight on d4
plans.description: Trade off White's dark-squared bishop, or plant a knight on d4 where no bind pawn can evict it, and live on the squares the bind pawns cannot touch.

success.note: RESTATED PLAN. The plan was 'Dark-square strategy', whose success was declined because the squares that matter shift. It is now the two concrete forms the plan itself names: White's dark-squared bishop is off the board, or a Black knight stands on d4 — the one square the bind's own pawns can never attack. Other dark squares are not counted. Original success note: 'Which dark squares matter shifts with the piece trades; no fixed square is honest.'

watch: White pawn control of b5 and d5 before either freeing break.
Every minor-piece trade: the bind squeezes less with each pair off.
The dark squares in front of the bind pawns once the c-pawns are gone.
typicalMistakes: Breaking with the b- or d-pawn before it is supported, trading a cramp for a permanent weakness.
Drifting without a break plan and slowly running out of squares.
Stretching the bind pawns forward until the dark squares behind them collapse.

Trigger basis: the shipped maroczy-bind catalogue convention (White pawns on c4 and e4, the d-file half-open for White, the c-file half-open for Black). The convention does not check Black's kingside arrangement or piece placement, so non-Sicilian positions matching the pawn signature also fire; the entry names the family, not the census.
